title: Unit Testing: mocking request.state

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
# This is as small as I can get it, sorry
from fastapi import Depends, APIRouter, Request, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

def some_dependency(request: Request):
    request.state.some_object = "state changed in dependency"

router = APIRouter(
    dependencies=[Depends(some_dependency)],
)

@router.get("/")
async def some_get(req: Request):
    return req.state.some_object

app.include_router(router)

---

test.py:

from unittest.mock import MagicMock
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection
from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient
import pytest
from main import app, some_dependency

pytestmark = [pytest.mark.anyio]

@pytest.fixture
def anyio_backend():
    return 'asyncio'


async def test_default_state():
    async with AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://example.com") as c:
        res =  await c.get("/")
        assert res.text == '"state changed in dependency"'

async def test_mock_state(monkeypatch):
    app.dependency_overrides[some_dependency] = lambda: MagicMock()
    mocked_object = MagicMock()
    mocked_object.some_object = "state changed in test"
    monkeypatch.setattr(HTTPConnection, "state", mocked_object)

    async with AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://example.com") as c:
        res =  await c.get("/")
        assert res.text == '"state changed in test"'
```


### Description

Is this the best way to mock State?
Without being able to change the real app I am testing to avoid using request.state, is this the best way to mock/patch FastAPI/Starlette?

I'm not sure how it would work, but a pytest decorator or fixture that allows state to be set up in tests would be excellent.

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.11

### Pydantic Version

2.10.6

### Python Version

3.13.2

### Additional Context

Checked: 
https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/9668
https://www.reddit.com/r/learnpython/comments/ygklcx/how_to_write_tests_for_fastapi_endpoints/ - I actually think this would work but didn't see it until later. If I stub out the dependency that would parse headers into state I am back to needing to patch the state in the test.
https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/5028 - I think this is basically what I've done to a different object

answer.body:
I think the best way is not to use `Request.state` directly in endpoint functions, but create dependencies to access variables you need.
Then you can just override those dependencies in a usual way
```
from fastapi import Depends, APIRouter, Request, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

def some_dependency(request: Request):
    request.state.some_object = "state changed in dependency"

router = APIRouter(
    dependencies=[Depends(some_dependency)],
)

async def get_some_object(req: Request):
    return req.state.some_object

@router.get("/")
async def some_get(some_object: Any = Depends(get_some_object)):
    return some_object

app.include_router(router)
```
